scenes.sub: A vault pools deposits and runs a strategy (often harvesting and reinvesting rewards). You get shares. Costs: performance fee (a share of profits), management fee (a share of assets per year), sometimes withdrawal fees. Risks: the vault's code plus every proto
scenes.vo: A vault pools deposits and runs a strategy (often harvesting and reinvesting rewards). You get shares. Costs: performance fee (a share of profits), management fee (a share of assets per year), sometimes withdrawal fees. Risks: the vault's code plus every protocol it uses.

scenes.title: Worked example
scenes.vo: Gross 10%, 20% performance fee, 0.5% management to 7.5% net. DIY instead, compounding weekly at $2 gas: $5,000 position: gas = $104 a year = 2.08% drag to the vault probably wins. $500,000 position: gas = 0.02% drag, while the vault's fees cost 2.5 points to DIY probably wins.
scenes.cap: $5,000 position: gas = $104/yr = 2.08% drag → the vault probably wins. $500,000 position: gas = 0.02% drag, while the vault's fees cost 2.5 points → DIY probably wins.

lines: Why do vaults suit small positions?
scenes.sub: Answer: They spread gas costs across all depositors.

lines: What risk does a vault add?
scenes.sub: Answer: Its own code and strategy, on top of every protocol it deposits into.
